subject: early-literacy
title: Letter sounds: a, b, c, d, e
summary: Learn the sound each of the first five letters makes, with words the child knows.

lesson.text: For a parent, older brother or sister, or anyone helping a young child: read this aloud and point at things around you.
Every letter has a name ("bee" for b) and a sound ("buh" for b). To read words, children need the sounds first. Say the sound short and clear, without a long "uh" at the end where you can.

items: b as in ball, bag, bread
c as in cat, cup, cake
d as in dog, drum, door

lesson.title: A sound game
steps: Say: "I spy something that starts with b."
The child looks around and points: "Ball!" or "Bag!"
Say the word slowly together: b... all. Hear the b at the start.

lesson.text: Write the letter big on paper or in sand. Let the child trace it with a finger while saying its sound.
Do a little every day. Five minutes of sounds each morning is better than one long lesson a week.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the sound "b"?
questions.explanation: Say it slowly: b... all. Ball starts with b. Cat starts with c, egg with e and dog with d.
Say it slowly: d... og. The first sound is d. The g is the last sound, not the first.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the same sound as "apple"?
questions.explanation: Apple and ant both start with the sound a.
Cup starts with the sound c, the same as cat and cake.
